flags.text: Describes the revisionist perspective as arguing that engagement 'can lead to' biased or antagonistic processing. The paper says engaged citizens 'may also be more likely to process information in biased or antagonistic ways' (p.2) and that engagement indicators 'can be associated with biased assessments' (p.4): an association tilted into an effect.

theoretical_positioning.note: Revisionist view of engagement (T2) extended to online political hostility (T3).

flags.text: Says grievance accounts hold that hostility is 'primarily driven' by marginalization, deprivation and status threat. The paper says these accounts 'focus on' or 'emphasize' them and that hostility 'may be connected to' deprivation (p.2-3).

interlocutor_claim.note: The grievance account (I3) without the paper's relation to it (it adds engagement as a further correlate).
Psychological account: antagonistic traits, sadism, situational triggers (p.2, the paper's 'often points to'); not the small-segment, extreme-traits claim, and no stance.
The classical view that engagement is a boon to democracy (p.4); the paper's qualifying stance is not stated.
